claim: During early mammalian development, the chromatin landscape undergoes profound transitions.
source: During early mammalian development, the chromatin landscape undergoes profound transitions.
evidence: This is a general statement about developmental biology that is supported by established scientific knowledge and is presented as background information.

claim: The Zdbf2 gene is involved in growth control.
source: The Zdbf2 gene—involved in growth control—provides a valuable model to study this window
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior work and established knowledge about Zdbf2 function.

claim: Upon exit from naïve pluripotency and prior to tissue differentiation, Zdbf2 undergoes a switch from a distal to a proximal promoter usage.
source: upon exit from naïve pluripotency and prior to tissue differentiation, it undergoes a switch from a distal to a proximal promoter usage
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript including RNA-seq and other molecular analyses.

claim: The Zdbf2 promoter switch is accompanied by a switch from polycomb to DNA methylation occupancy.
source: accompanied by a switch from polycomb to DNA methylation occupancy
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq and WGBS data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Four enhancers contribute to the Zdbf2 promoter switch.
source: we show here that four enhancers contribute to the Zdbf2 promoter switch
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP, and deletion experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Zdbf2 promoter switch occurs concomitantly with dynamic changes in chromatin architecture.
source: we show here that four enhancers contribute to the Zdbf2 promoter switch, concomitantly with dynamic changes in chromatin architecture
evidence: This is supported by 4C-seq data showing changes in chromatin interactions during differentiation.

claim: In ESCs, the Zdbf2 locus is partitioned to facilitate enhancer contacts with the distal Zdbf2 promoter.
source: In ESCs, the locus is partitioned to facilitate enhancer contacts with the distal Zdbf2 promoter.
evidence: This is supported by 4C-seq data and CTCF ChIP experiments showing CTCF-mediated partitioning.

claim: Relieving the partition enhances proximal Zdbf2 promoter activity.
source: Relieving the partition enhances proximal Zdbf2 promoter activity, as observed during differentiation or with genetic mutants.
evidence: This is supported by deletion experiments of the CTCF partition site and observations during differentiation.

claim: 3D regulation occurs upstream of the polycomb and DNA methylation pathways.
source: Importantly, we show that 3D regulation occurs upstream of the polycomb and DNA methylation pathways.
evidence: This is supported by experiments showing that chromatin architecture changes occur independently of DNA methylation and polycomb status.

claim: During the naïve-to-primed transition, pluripotent cells transition from globally low DNA methylation to highly DNA methylated states.
source: One hallmark of the naïve pluripotent state is globally low DNA methylation, whereas primed cells are highly DNA methylated (Seisenberger et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Seisenberger et al., 2012).

claim: Chromatin architecture and histone modifications are dramatically remodeled during the naïve-to-primed transition.
source: Incidentally, chromatin architecture and the underlying histone modifications are also dramatically remodeled during this period (Lee et al., 2014; Xu and Xie, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Lee et al., 2014; Xu and Xie, 2018).

claim: Oct4 relies on naïve and primed cell-specific enhancers.
source: Notably, the general regulator of pluripotency Oct4 (also known as Pou5f1) relies on an naïve and primed cell-specific enhancers (Tesar et al., 2007; Yeom et al., 1996)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Tesar et al., 2007; Yeom et al., 1996).

claim: The developmental regulator Nodal relies on naïve and primed cell-specific enhancers.
source: as does the developmental regulator Nodal (Papanayotou et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Papanayotou et al., 2014).

claim: GRHL2 coordinates enhancer switches for epithelial genes by activating the primed set of enhancers during differentiation.
source: Recently, it was demonstrated that the transcription factor GRHL2 coordinates a large set of these enhancer switches for epithelial genes by activating the primed set of enhancers during differentiation (Chen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Chen et al., 2018).

claim: In the naïve state, the distal Long isoform of Zdbf2 promoter (pLiz) is active.
source: In the naïve state, the distal Long isoform of Zdbf2 promoter (pLiz) is active.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: As cells exit naïve pluripotency, a promoter switch occurs, resulting in activation of the proximal Zdbf2 promoter (pZdbf2), located 73 kilobases downstream.
source: As cells exit naïve pluripotency, a promoter switch occurs, resulting in activation of the proximal Zdbf2 promoter (pZdbf2), located 73 kilobases (kb) downstream.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data and genomic mapping presented in the manuscript.

claim: From the primed state and throughout life, pZdbf2 is the functional promoter while pLiz is constitutively silenced.
source: From the primed state and then throughout life, pZdbf2 is the functional promoter while pLiz is constitutively silenced.
evidence: This is supported by prior work and data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Despite the genomic distance, there is no change in the message between the Liz and Zdbf2 isoforms.
source: It should be noted that despite the genomic distance, there is no change in the message between the Liz and Zdbf2 isoforms, thus the promoter switch does not result in protein diversity.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the gene structure and transcript sequences.

claim: pLiz activity is absolutely required for imprinted deposition of DNA methylation at a somatic differentially methylated region (sDMR).
source: pLiz activity is absolutely required for imprinted deposition of DNA methylation at a somatic differentially methylated region (sDMR).
evidence: This is supported by prior work cited in the manuscript (Duffié et al., 2014; Greenberg et al., 2017).

claim: The sDMR DNA methylation antagonizes a block of polycomb-mediated repression, freeing pZdbf2.
source: The sDMR DNA methylation, in turn, antagonizes a block of polycomb-mediated repression, freeing pZdbf2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Duffié et al., 2014; Greenberg et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by prior work cited in the manuscript and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Mice that are deficient for pLiz are never able to activate pZdbf2, leading to a substantial growth defect.
source: Mice that are deficient for pLiz are never able to activate pZdbf2, and this leads to a substantial growth defect.
evidence: This is supported by prior work on mouse models.

claim: Four prominent ATAC-seq peaks of accessible chromatin (E1 to E4) lie between pLiz and pZdbf2 promoters.
source: Four prominent ATAC-seq peaks of accessible chromatin (E1 to E4) lie between pLiz and pZdbf2 promoters.
evidence: This is directly shown in the ATAC-seq data presented in Figure 1A.

claim: E1-3 are enriched for H3K27ac in both ESCs and D7 EpiLCs.
source: E1-3 appeared enriched for the H3K27ac mark in both cell types
evidence: This is shown by H3K27ac ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 1B.

claim: E4 is enriched for H3K27ac only in D7 EpiLCs.
source: while E4 was enriched for the mark only in D7 EpiLCs (Figure 1B)
evidence: This is shown by H3K27ac ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 1B.

claim: E1-3 can be classified as active enhancers in ESCs and EpiLCs.
source: Thus, while E1-3 can be classified as active in ESCs and EpiLCs
evidence: This is based on H3K27ac enrichment and chromatin accessibility data.

claim: The chromatin accessibility and H3K27ac dynamics at E4 are reminiscent of 'poised' enhancers.
source: the chromatin accessibility and H3K27ac dynamics at E4 are reminiscent of so-called 'poised' enhancers (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) (Buecker et al., 2014; Rada-Iglesias et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by comparison with known poised enhancers and citations to prior work (Buecker et al., 2014; Rada-Iglesias et al., 2011).

claim: E4 is marked by P300 in ESCs.
source: Moreover, publicly available data indicate that E4 is marked by P300 in ESCs
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B using publicly available data.

claim: E4 shows high levels of vertebrate conservation.
source: and shows high levels of vertebrate conservation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B using PhastCons data.

claim: OCT4 is enriched at all of the putative enhancers in both naïve ESCs and D7 EpiLCs.
source: OCT4 is enriched at all of the putative enhancers in both naïve ESCs and D7 EpiLCs (two pluripotent cell types)
evidence: This is based on publicly available ChIP-seq data (Buecker et al., 2014).

claim: Both classes of enhancers are likely regulated in a pluripotency-dependent manner.
source: indicating that both classes of enhancers are likely regulated in a pluripotency-dependent manner (Buecker et al., 2014)
evidence: This is inferred from OCT4 binding data and citation to prior work.

claim: The in vivo and in cellula regulation of the Zdbf2 locus are coherent.
source: suggesting that the in vivo and in cellula regulation are coherent (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B) (Liu et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by comparison of in vivo ICM data with ESC data, with citations to prior work (Liu et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2016).

claim: The Zdbf2 locus exists within an 'inter-TAD' that spans ~650 kb.
source: available Hi-C data from mouse ESCs indicates that the Zdbf2 locus exists within an 'inter-TAD' that spans ~650 kb (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A) (Bonev et al., 2017)
evidence: This is based on published Hi-C data (Bonev et al., 2017) shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The inter-TAD can be subdivided, with intra-Zdbf2 locus and intra-Adam23 locus interactions occurring in relatively mutually exclusive domains.
source: Our 4C-seq data further allowed us to subdivide this inter-TAD, with intra-Zdbf2 locus and intra-Adam23 locus interactions occurring in relatively mutually exclusive domains (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is based on 4C-seq data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: In ESCs, when Liz is expressed, the pLiz promoter exhibits increased interactions with the E1-3 cluster relative to EpiLCs.
source: However, in ESCs, when Liz is expressed, the pLiz promoter did exhibit increased interactions with the E1-3 cluster relative to EpiLCs
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 1C.

claim: E1-3 contribute to pLiz regulation.
source: This is consistent with the possibility that E1-3 contribute to pLiz regulation.
evidence: This is inferred from 4C-seq interaction data and H3K27ac enrichment.

claim: No marked looping occurs between pLiz and E4 in either ESCs or D7 EpiLCs.
source: No marked looping appeared to occur between pLiz and E4 in either ESCs or D7 EpiLCs.
evidence: This is based on 4C-seq data analysis.

claim: pZdbf2 exhibits increased contacts with all four of the putative enhancers in D7 EpiLCs.
source: Our 4C-seq revealed that pZdbf2 exhibited increased contacts with all four of the putative enhancers in D7 EpiLCs (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 1C.

claim: E1-4 have a potential cooperative role in activating pZdbf2.
source: This indicates a potential cooperative role for E1-4 in activating pZdbf2.
evidence: This is inferred from the 4C-seq interaction data showing increased contacts in EpiLCs.

claim: Deleting the E3 element has no impact on expression or DNA methylation at the Zdbf2 locus.
source: As such, deleting the element had no impact on expression or DNA methylation at the Zdbf2 locus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR and bisulfite sequencing data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: In the absence of E1-3, the Liz transcript is markedly repressed.
source: In the absence of these elements, the Liz transcript was markedly repressed
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 2C.

claim: In the absence of E1-3, the canonical Zdbf2 isoform fails to properly activate.
source: and the canonical Zdbf2 isoform failed to properly activate (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 2C.

claim: E1-3 are enhancers of pLiz.
source: However, the data provide a strong indication that E1-3 are indeed enhancers of pLiz.
evidence: This is inferred from deletion experiments showing reduced Liz expression.

claim: In the absence of E1-3, DNA methylation accumulates faster at pLiz.
source: Interestingly, in the absence of E1-3, DNA methylation accumulated faster at pLiz
evidence: This is shown by bisulfite pyrosequencing data in Figure 2D.

claim: In the absence of E1-3, DNA methylation fails to properly accumulate at the sDMR region, reaching 67% by D7.
source: In the absence of E1-3, DNA methylation failed to properly accumulate at the sDMR region, reaching 67% by D7 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is shown by bisulfite pyrosequencing data in Figure 2D.

claim: ΔE4 mutant cells exhibit no alteration of Liz expression.
source: Indeed, ∆E4 mutant cells exhibited no alteration of Liz expression
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 2F.

claim: In ΔE4 mutant cells, Zdbf2 transcripts are strongly reduced.
source: but Zdbf2 transcripts were strongly reduced (Figure 2F)
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 2F.

claim: The ΔE4 mutation has no impact on DNA methylation at the Zdbf2 locus.
source: As Liz was unaffected, there was no impact on DNA methylation at the locus (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is shown by bisulfite pyrosequencing data in Figure 2G.

claim: Reduced expression of Zdbf2 in ΔE4 EpiLCs does not correlate with maintained polycomb occupancy in the sDMR region and pZdbf2.
source: Moreover, reduced expression of Zdbf2 in ∆E4 EpiLCs did not correlate with maintained polycomb occupancy in the sDMR region and pZdbf2 (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is shown by H3K27me3 ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 2H.

claim: The enhancer E4 is necessary for pZdbf2 activation, irrespective of the local DNA methylation or polycomb status.
source: In sum, the enhancer E4 is necessary for pZdbf2 activation, irrespective of the local DNA methylation or polycomb status.
evidence: This is inferred from the ΔE4 deletion experiments showing reduced Zdbf2 expression without changes in DNA methylation or polycomb.

claim: E4 is depleted for H3K27me3.
source: whereas E4 is depleted for the mark (Figure 2H)
evidence: This is shown by H3K27me3 ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 2H.

claim: E4 is relatively depleted for H3K27me2.
source: Yet H3K27me2 ChIP analysis revealed that E4 is relatively depleted for this mark as well (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown by H3K27me2 ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Deleting E4 results in a slight increase of H3K27me3 enrichment 1 kb upstream of the WT polycomb domain.
source: deleting E4 resulted in a slight increase of H3K27me3 enrichment 1 kb upstream of the WT polycomb domain
evidence: This is shown by H3K27me3 ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 2H.

claim: In Eed mutant ESCs, there is precocious activation of pZdbf2.
source: We previously showed that in ESCs containing loss-of-function mutations in the Embryonic ectoderm development (Eed) gene (Schoeftner et al., 2006)—a core component of PRC2—there was precocious activation of pZdbf2 (Greenberg et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by prior work cited in the manuscript (Greenberg et al., 2017).

claim: In the absence of polycomb-mediated repression in ESCs, both E4 and pZdbf2 become enriched for H3K27ac.
source: Indeed, both E4 and pZdbf2 became enriched for H3K27ac in the absence of polycomb-mediated repression in ESCs (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is shown by H3K27ac ChIP-qPCR data in Eed-/- ESCs in Figure 3A.

claim: pLiz and E1-3 exhibit no significant change in H3K27ac in Eed mutant ESCs.
source: Incidentally, pLiz and E1-3, which are already active in ESCs, exhibited no significant change.
evidence: This is shown by H3K27ac ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 3A.

claim: In ΔLiz mutants, the E4 enhancer does not attain complete levels of H3K27ac during EpiLC differentiation.
source: As such, in the ∆Liz mutant, the E4 enhancer did not attain complete levels of H3K27ac during EpiLC differentiation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is shown by H3K27ac ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 3B.

claim: E4 activity is controlled in a polycomb-dependent manner.
source: Thus, while E4 does not display the signatures of direct polycomb regulation, per se, its activity is controlled in a polycomb-dependent manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the H3K27ac ChIP data in Eed mutants and ΔLiz mutants.

claim: In Eed mutant ESCs, pZdbf2 exhibits increased interactions at E4, but not E1-3.
source: In Eed mutants, pZdbf2 exhibits increased interactions at E4, but not E1-3.
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 3C.

claim: In the absence of Liz transcription, there is only a minor effect on the distal interaction landscape of pZdbf2.
source: However, our 4C-seq analysis revealed that in the absence of Liz transcription, there is only a minor effect on the distal interaction landscape of pZdbf2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In ΔLiz EpiLCs, pZdbf2 exhibits increased interactions with E1-4, but not to the same extent as WT EpiLCs.
source: Moreover, in ∆Liz EpiLCs, pZdbf2 exhibited increased interactions with E1-4, but not to the same extent as WT EpiLCs.
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The polycomb region that regulates pZdbf2 spans ~25 kb, from E4 and into the body of Zdbf2.
source: The polycomb region that regulates pZdbf2 spans ~ 25 kb, from E4 and into the body of Zdbf2 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is shown by H3K27me3 ChIP-seq data in Figure 1A.

claim: In ESCs, the polycomb region forms a tightly packed domain.
source: Consistent with previous reports, in ESCs this region forms a tightly packed domain (Kundu et al., 2017) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 1C and supported by citation to prior work (Kundu et al., 2017).

claim: In PRC2 mutant ESCs, pZdbf2 interacts even more frequently within the domain normally defined by a polycomb block in WT cells.
source: In fact, in a PRC2 mutant, pZdbf2 interacted even more frequently within the domain normally defined by a polycomb block in WT cells.
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 3C.

claim: In Eed mutant ESCs, pZdbf2 does not exhibit increased interactions with E1-3.
source: However, our 4C-seq in the polycomb mutant showed that this was not the case (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 3C.

claim: Liz transcription and the polycomb status play a limited role in the regulation of the pZdbf2 interaction landscape in ESCs.
source: To summarize, Liz transcription and the polycomb status play a limited role in the regulation of the pZdbf2 interaction landscape in ESCs, and there must be other mechanisms in place.
evidence: This is inferred from 4C-seq data in ΔLiz and Eed mutant cells.

claim: In ESCs, a CTCF-binding site proximal to the Gpr1 promoter forms a looping structure with two CTCF sites downstream of the Gpr1 gene.
source: In ESCs, a CTCF-binding site proximal to the Gpr1 promoter formed a looping structure with two CTCF sites downstream of the Gpr1 gene (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 4A.

claim: pLiz and E1-3 co-reside within the genomic segment defined by the CTCF loop.
source: Incidentally, pLiz and E1-3 co-reside within this genomic segment.
evidence: This is inferred from the 4C-seq data showing the loop structure.

claim: During differentiation to EpiLCs, the pLiz/E1-3 interactions are reduced.
source: During differentiation to EpiLCs, we found that the pLiz/E1-3 interactions are reduced.
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 4A.

claim: CTCF binding at the partition site depletes during differentiation, whereas CTCF remains bound at the sites downstream of Gpr1.
source: In accordance, CTCF binding at this site depleted, whereas CTCF remained bound at the sites downstream of Gpr1 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by CTCF ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 4B.

claim: The CTCF partition site physically separates the active pLiz/E1-3 region from the silent pZdbf2/E4 region in ESCs.
source: Therefore, we referred to this binding platform as the 'CTCF_partition site' (CTCF_PS), which physically separates the active pLiz/E1-3 region from the silent pZdbf2/E4 region in ESCs (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is inferred from 4C-seq and CTCF ChIP data, illustrated in Figure 4C.

claim: In EpiLCs, disappearance of CTCF at the partition site allows for pZdbf2 to interact with E1-3, while pLiz is silenced.
source: In EpiLCs, disappearance of CTCF at the partition site would then allow for pZdbf2 to interact with E1-3, while pLiz is silenced.
evidence: This is inferred from the CTCF ChIP and 4C-seq data.

claim: The partition loop still forms in absence of polycomb in Eed mutant ESCs.
source: Using the CTCF_PS as a VP in our Eed mutant ESCs, we observed that the partition loop still formed in absence of polycomb (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CTCF remains enriched at the CTCF_PS in PRC2 mutant ESCs.
source: Furthermore, CTCF still remained enriched at the CTCF_PS in PRC2 mutant ESCs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by CTCF ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 4B.

claim: Even in the absence of DNA methylation, CTCF depletes at the partition site during differentiation.
source: However, even in the absence of DNA methylation, CTCF depleted at the partition site (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown by CTCF ChIP-qPCR data in Dnmt tKO cells in Figure 4D.

claim: CTCF depletion at the CTCF_PS occurs even in the absence of the Liz transcript.
source: yet we observed reduced CTCF enrichment even in the absence of the Liz transcript (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is shown by CTCF ChIP-qPCR data in ΔLiz cells in Figure 4D.

claim: The CTCF depletion at the CTCF_PS in EpiLCs is differentiation-dependent, but independent of DNA methylation- or Liz transcription-based regulation.
source: Therefore, the CTCF depletion at the CTCF_PS in EpiLCs is differentiation-dependent, but independent of DNA methylation- or Liz transcription-based regulation.
evidence: This is inferred from CTCF ChIP data in Dnmt tKO and ΔLiz cells.

claim: In ΔCTCF_PS cells, pLiz interacts less frequently with E1-3 in ESCs.
source: 4C-seq in ∆CTCF_PS cells revealed that pLiz interacts less frequently with E1-3 in ESCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B)
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: In ΔCTCF_PS mutant ESCs, Liz fails to properly express.
source: As such, Liz failed to properly express (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 4E.

claim: The ΔCTCF_PS deletion does not perturb expression of Gpr1 nor the genes flanking the Zdbf2 locus.
source: In contrast, the deletion did not perturb expression of Gpr1 nor the genes flanking the Zdbf2 locus (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C)
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: During differentiation of the ΔCTCF_PS line, the Liz transcript is able to attain WT levels, but Zdbf2 fails to properly activate.
source: During differentiation of the ∆CTCF_PS line, the Liz transcript was still able to attain WT levels, nevertheless Zdbf2 failed to properly activate (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 4E.

claim: In ΔCTCF_PS mutants, DNA methylation occurs normally at pLiz, but the sDMR remains relatively hypomethylated compared to WT.
source: Moreover, while DNA methylation occurred normally at pLiz, the sDMR remained relatively hypomethylated compared to WT (Figure 4F)
evidence: This is shown by bisulfite pyrosequencing data in Figure 4F.

claim: The relative reduction of DNA methylation at the sDMR in ΔCTCF_PS mutant EpiLCs is correlated with a slight retention of H3K27me3 in comparison with WT.
source: Furthermore, the relative reduction of DNA methylation at the sDMR in ∆CTCF_PS mutant EpiLCs was correlated with a slight retention of H3K27me3 in comparison with WT
evidence: This is shown by H3K27me3 ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A.

claim: In ΔCTCF_PS mutant ESCs, pZdbf2 exhibits increased contacts with E2 and E3.
source: While pLiz activation was less efficient in ∆CTCF_PS mutant ESCs, pZdbf2 exhibited increased contacts with E2 and E3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: In ΔCTCF_PS mutant ESCs, Zdbf2 remains repressed, as polycomb enrichment remains unperturbed.
source: However, Zdbf2 remained repressed, as polycomb enrichment remained unperturbed (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is shown by H3K27me3 ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Upon global depletion of CTCF, Zdbf2 is de-repressed.
source: It should be noted that upon global depletion of CTCF, Zdbf2 is de-repressed, indicating that independently of the partition site, CTCF does play a role in Zdbf2 regulation in ESCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in CTCF degron cells in Figure 4—figure supplement 2E.

claim: While Zdbf2 is upregulated in absence of Eed alone, the expression is significantly increased in the ΔCTCF-PS; Eed-/- double mutant.
source: Indeed, while Zdbf2 was upregulated in absence of Eed alone, the expression was significantly increased in the ∆CTCF-PS; Eed-/- double mutant (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 4G.

claim: In ΔCTCF_PS mutants, there is a further increase of Zdbf2 de-repression when H3K27me3 is depleted with EZH2 inhibitor.
source: Importantly, these results were confirmed when we subjected WT and ∆CTCF_PS lines to a potent PRC2 inhibitor to induce acute depletion of H3K27me3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3D,E).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 4—figure supplement 3E.

claim: The CTCF partition acts as a second level of protection, along with polycomb, to restrain precocious pZdbf2 firing.
source: Therefore, we concluded that in addition to contributing to proper pLiz activation, the CTCF partition acts as a second level of protection, along with polycomb, to restrain precocious pZdbf2 firing.
evidence: This is inferred from the genetic experiments showing additive effects of CTCF partition deletion and polycomb loss.

claim: A CTCF-structured loop organization forms at the Zdbf2 locus in naïve ESCs.
source: Here we show that a CTCF-structured loop organization forms at the locus in naïve ESCs.
evidence: This is shown by 4C-seq and CTCF ChIP data.

claim: The CTCF partition allows for proper regulation of pLiz.
source: This partition allows for proper regulation of pLiz
evidence: This is inferred from deletion experiments showing reduced Liz expression in ΔCTCF_PS mutants.

claim: pLiz can facilitate a local polycomb-to-DNA methylation switch through Liz transcription.
source: which in turn can facilitate a local polycomb-to-DNA methylation switch through Liz transcription
evidence: This is supported by prior work and data in the manuscript.

claim: During differentiation, the CTCF partitioning is relaxed, as pLiz becomes shut down, allowing distal enhancers to bolster pZdbf2 activation.
source: During differentiation, the partitioning is relaxed, as pLiz becomes shut down, thus allowing distal enhancers to bolster pZdbf2 activation.
evidence: This is inferred from 4C-seq and CTCF ChIP data showing loss of CTCF binding and increased pZdbf2-enhancer interactions.

claim: E1-3 may act in a hierarchical manner with respect to E4 and pZdbf2, being important for activation of the proximal promoter rather than sustaining Zdbf2 expression.
source: It is conceivable that E1-3 act in a hierarchical manner with respect to E4 and pZdbf2; that is, they are important for activation of the proximal promoter rather than sustaining Zdbf2 expression, although further testing must be performed to formally confirm his possibility.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observed interaction patterns and deletion phenotypes.

claim: Deleting the CTCF_PS results in reduced Liz activation kinetics, but a fairly substantial effect on Zdbf2 expression.
source: Deleting the CTCF_PS resulted in reduced Liz activation kinetics, but a fairly substantial effect on Zdbf2 expression.
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in ΔCTCF_PS mutants.

claim: The sensitivity of pZdbf2 activity to proper epigenetic programming is underscored by the effects of CTCF partition deletion.
source: Such results underscore the sensitivity of pZdbf2 activity to proper epigenetic programming.
evidence: This is inferred from the substantial effects on Zdbf2 expression despite moderate effects on Liz and DNA methylation.

claim: In ΔCTCF_PS ESCs, Zdbf2 transcription does not ectopically occur, even though there are no longer apparent restrictions for pZdbf2 to interact with the active enhancers E1-3.
source: In ∆CTCF_PS ESCs, Zdbf2 transcription did not ectopically occur, even though there were no longer apparent restrictions for pZdbf2 to interact with the active enhancers E1-3.
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR and 4C-seq data in ΔCTCF_PS mutants.

claim: Polycomb-mediated silencing persists over pZdbf2 in the absence of CTCF_PS.
source: The explanation for this is the polycomb-mediated silencing that persists over pZdbf2 in the absence of CTCF_PS.
evidence: This is shown by H3K27me3 ChIP data in ΔCTCF_PS mutants.

claim: There are at least two layers of regulation of Zdbf2 activation that act independently from classical transcription factor control at gene promoters: instructive chromosome conformation and a Liz-dependent epigenetic switch.
source: Thus, there are at least two layers of regulation of Zdbf2 activation that act independently from classical transcription factor control at gene promoters: 1) instructive chromosome conformation allowing for proper pLiz and pZdfb2 activity, and 2) a Liz-dependent epigenetic switch to evict polycomb at pZdbf2.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined genetic and molecular data showing independent contributions of chromatin architecture and epigenetic marks.

claim: Chromosome conformation acts upstream in the tiered regulatory model of Zdbf2.
source: This tiered model, with chromosome conformation acting upstream, emphasizes the exquisite choreography that can occur to program developmentally important genes during the exit from the naïve pluripotent state.
evidence: This is inferred from the epistatic relationship between 3D organization and epigenetic marks.

claim: Global depletion of CTCF leads to upregulation of Zdbf2 in ESCs.
source: Interestingly, global depletion of CTCF leads to upregulation of Zdbf2 in ESCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in CTCF degron cells in Figure 4—figure supplement 2E.

claim: CTCF is generally reported to be largely invariant across mammalian cell types.
source: While CTCF is generally reported to be largely invariant across mammalian cell types (Lee et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Lee et al., 2012).

claim: There are cell type-specific CTCF binding patterns, and roughly 60% occur in a DNA methylation-independent manner.
source: there are cell type-specific CTCF binding patterns, and roughly 60% occur in a DNA methylation-independent manner (Wang et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Wang et al., 2012).

claim: The Zdbf2 locus presents a case of two alternative promoters utilizing a shared set of enhancers in a CTCF-guided, developmentally timed manner.
source: Our study presents a rare description of two alternative promoters utilizing a shared set of enhancers, but in a CTCF-guided, developmentally timed manner.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the combined data in the manuscript.

claim: In ESCs, CTCF is required to facilitate pLiz interactions while restricting pZdbf2 interactions.
source: In ESCs, CTCF is required to facilitate one promoter's interactions (pLiz) while restricting the other's (pZdbf2).
evidence: This is inferred from 4C-seq and deletion data showing differential effects on the two promoters.

claim: Only upon removal of CTCF binding, the opportunity for pZdbf2 is created to contact its enhancers.
source: Only upon removal of CTCF binding, the opportunity for pZdbf2 is created to contact its enhancers.
evidence: This is inferred from CTCF ChIP and 4C-seq data during differentiation.

claim: At the imprinted Igf2/H19 locus, CTCF binding near the H19 gene on the maternal allele restricts interactions between a shared set of enhancers and the more distal Igf2 gene.
source: On the face of it, such a mechanism resembles the imprinted Igf2/H19 locus, where CTCF binding near the H19 gene on the maternal allele restrict interactions between a shared set of enhancers and the more distal Igf2 gene (Murrell et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Murrell et al., 2004).

claim: The Igf2/H19 locus behaves differently from the Zdbf2 locus, as differential CTCF binding is DNA methylation-dependent and set in the gametes.
source: The Igf2/H19 locus behaves differently from the Zdbf2 locus, though, as differential CTCF binding is DNA methylation-dependent and set in the gametes—not dynamically regulated during cellular differentiation.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about Igf2/H19 regulation.

claim: Igf2 and H19 are two different genes, not isoforms of the same gene.
source: Moreover, Igf2 and H19 are two different genes, not isoforms of the same gene.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about gene structure.

claim: At the Hoxd locus in mice, CTCF facilitates the interactions between the same set of gene promoters but different sets of enhancers depending on the context.
source: For example, at the Hoxd locus in mice, CTCF facilitates the interactions between the same set of gene promoters but different sets of enhancers depending on the context (Andrey et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Andrey et al., 2013).

claim: Promoter switching is a widespread and developmentally important phenomenon.
source: Promoter switching is a widespread and developmentally important phenomenon (Davuluri et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Davuluri et al., 2008).

claim: Aberrant promoter usage is associated with pathologies, such as cancer.
source: Aberrant promoter usage is associated with pathologies, such as cancer (Sarda et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Sarda et al., 2017).

claim: CTCF is a likely candidate to organize genic three-dimensional structure and protect from aberrant promoter firing.
source: CTCF is a likely candidate to organize genic three-dimensional structure and protect from aberrant promoter firing, as it does at Zdbf2.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing CTCF's role in organizing the Zdbf2 locus.

claim: If pLiz-to-pZdbf2 promoter switch does not occur at the proper developmental time, synchronized with the de novo DNA methylation program, pZdbf2 cannot be activated.
source: The Zdbf2 locus presents a compelling case, because if pLiz-to-pZdbf2 promoter switch does not occur at the proper developmental time, synchronized with the de novo DNA methylation program, pZdbf2 cannot be activated (Greenberg et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by prior work cited in the manuscript (Greenberg et al., 2017).

claim: The organization of the Zdbf2 locus is conserved between mouse and humans.
source: Notably, the organization of this locus is conserved between mouse and humans, implying the likelihood of a shared regulatory mechanism (Duffié et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Duffié et al., 2014).

claim: The pLiz ATAC-seq peak diminishes as it becomes repressed and DNA methylated from ESCs to D7 EpiLCs.
source: As expected, the ATAC-Seq peak for pLiz diminished as it became repressed and DNA methylated from ESCs to D7 EpiLCs.
evidence: This is shown by ATAC-seq data in Figure 1A.

claim: An ATAC-Seq peak is present at pZdbf2 in ESCs and further enhanced in D7 EpiLCs.
source: An ATAC-Seq peak was present at pZdbf2 in ESCs and further enhanced in D7 EpiLCs
evidence: This is shown by ATAC-seq data in Figure 1A.

claim: pZdbf2 is bivalent and poised in ESCs.
source: this is correlated with our previous data indicating that pZdbf2 is bivalent and poised in ESCs (Greenberg et al., 2017; Mas et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Greenberg et al., 2017; Mas et al., 2018).

claim: In the ESC-to-EpiLC cellular system, the imprinted status of the Zdbf2 locus is lost.
source: In this cellular system, the imprinted status of the locus is lost
evidence: This is based on prior characterization of the cell system.

claim: The ESC-to-EpiLC cellular system biallelically recapitulates all events occurring in vivo on the paternal allele, including the pLiz to pZdbf2 promoter usage switch and sDMR methylation.
source: but it biallelically recapitulates all events occurring in vivo on the paternal allele, including the pLiz to pZdbf2 promoter usage switch and sDMR methylation (Greenberg et al., 2017)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Greenberg et al., 2017).

claim: D4 and D7 EpiLCs cluster more closely with EpiSCs than with earlier time points, indicating a primed pluripotency state.
source: In comparison with publicly available data (Bao et al., 2018), D4 and D7 EpiLCs cluster more closely with EpiSCs, indicating a primed pluripotency state.
evidence: This is shown by hierarchical clustering analysis in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Upregulation of markers of primed pluripotency indicates that D7 EpiLCs have entered a primed pluripotency state.
source: Upregulation of markers of primed pluripotency indicate that D7 EpiLCs have entered a primed pluripotency state.
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The pLiz-to-pZdbf2 promoter switch occurs at roughly D4 of EpiLC differentiation.
source: The pLiz-to-pZdbf2 promoter switch occurs at roughly D4.
evidence: This is shown by expression dynamics data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: pLiz is shut down and pZdbf2 is active by D7 of EpiLC differentiation.
source: pLiz is shut down and pZdbf2 is active by D7.
evidence: This is shown by expression dynamics data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.
